top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye. The magic-wavelength lattice is an original invention distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. It is experimentally verified: Sr, Yb and Hg clocks in several independent laboratories agree near 1e-18, and it has already opened new physics (gravitational redshift at mm scale, constant-drift bounds, many-body effects). The two roles, Katori's proposal and first realization and Ye's drive to record accuracy and many-body use, are separable, so the two-name allocation is clean. I would keep the citation on the invention and realization, not on accuracy or on the redefinition of the second. No award is ranked second only because the criteria are met.
